coverage.summary: Applies to residential tenancies under a written lease, with no unit-count, building-age or owner limits stated. Tenancies at will are handled separately in § 12.
coverage.other_conditions: Tenancy must be under a written lease.

evidence.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease

result.notes: I removed 'nonpayment of rent' from other_conditions. It is the event that triggers the rule (tenant conduct), not a coverage attribute of the building, unit or owner. The only coverage limit in § 11 is that the tenancy be under a written lease. The statute states no unit-count, construction-date or owner-type limits. Tenancies at will are covered by the separate § 12 (D051). Nothing in the documents makes the rule depend on facts assessor data cannot show beyond lease form, so no exemptions are listed. As the existing review note says, this is a notice-to-quit rule, not a just-cause list.
